articles.title: French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit
articles.description: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living.

articles.title: Russian elections a ‘veneer of democracy’ with opposition barred from running
articles.description: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, September 18: Russia holds its first parliamentary elections since the Ukraine war. Since only parties loyal to Vladimir Putin are running, the elections are seen as nothing but a veneer of democracy. In sports: Zinedine Zidane will unveil his first selection as coach of the French football team. Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic organisers approve a croc-infested river to hold canoe and rowing events. Finally, the first new feline species in a century has been discover

articles.title: France’s Macron summons party leaders for talks on Mideast and Ukraine
articles.description: French President Emmanuel Macron is meeting leaders of France’s political parties at the Elysée on Friday for talks on the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine and the consequences for the country’s security and energy amid soaring fuel prices.

articles.title: Russia votes in wartime election set to secure the Kremlin's power
articles.description: Voting got ⁠underway on Friday in a tightly controlled three-day parliamentary election in Russia which President Vladimir Putin has framed as a barometer of support for Russia's war in Ukraine. It is the first parliamentary election since Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022, and most anti-war candidates have been excluded from the ballot.

articles.title: Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race
articles.description: French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents.

related.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Éric Zemmour confirme qu'il sera candidat, durcit encore son discours sur l'immigration
related.description: Sur BFMTV, le président de Reconquête a déroulé les éléments de son programme politique. Partisan de la «remigration», Éric Zemmour a fixé à un an la durée de chômage après laquelle un étranger, même en situation régulière, devrait être contraint de quitter la France.

articles.title: Russia seizes assets of Swiss food giant Nestle and three French firms
articles.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree on Thursday to transfer assets of Swiss food giant Nestle and three French groups to a company called LEV Management. Most Western companies quickly sold their Russian operations and holdings after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and the Kremlin has since made it difficult for firms to leave the country.

articles.title: L'objectif de 5% de déficit en 2027 fixé par le gouvernement pour le budget est "ambitieux" mais "évidemment réalisable", assure le ministre de l'Economie
articles.description: La cible de 5% de déficit "veut dire des efforts importants partout, pour l'Etat, pour les collectivités locales et pour les administrations de Sécurité sociale", a expliqué Roland Lescure, alors que son Premier ministre a présenté un budget contenant 54 milliards d'économies.

Il avait menacé quelques jours plus tôt la chaîne de poursuites pénales si elle continuait à faire intervenir Xenia Fedorova, collaboratrice russe pro-Kremlin expulsée fin juillet.

articles.title: US approves $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 warplanes to Saudi Arabia
articles.description: The United States on Thursday said it had approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 stealth warplanes to Saudi Arabia. Israel has previously voiced concerns about Riyadh buying F-35s, despite a push to normalise relations.

articles.title: Japon : l'inflation ralentit légèrement en août

articles.description: Les Gardiens de la révolution iraniens ont annoncé vendredi avoir frappé un pétrolier battant pavillon togolais dans le secteur du détroit d’Ormuz.

articles.title: France’s Yellow Vests to return as fuel prices soar?
articles.description: Eight years after fuel taxes helped spark the Yellow Vest movement, calls for a return to the streets are gathering momentum in France amid soaring energy prices. As governments and businesses look to harness the technology, concerns are growing over jobs, misinformation and the need for safeguards.

articles.title: Venezuela lifts block on some news sites as transition talks resume
articles.description: Venezuela has unblocked some news sites that had been censored for years, its telecom regulator said Thursday, as US-backed political transition talks were set to resume. Digital rights group VE Sin Filtro verified access to 17 news sites through several internet providers. However, at least 188 websites remain blocked, it said, including 79 news outlets.

articles.title: Police move hundreds of migrants still in Ceuta off beaches in Spanish enclave
